title: Lions and cheetahs and chimps, oh my: A spotlight on Africa's diverse wildlife
gist: Ars Technica profiles National Geographic's seven-episode Africa: Earth's Wild Home, a four-year, nearly 30-country production meant to launch a seven-continent franchise now on Disney+ and Hulu. It highlights field use of drones and a robotic camera arm, with narrator Wunmi Mosaku discussing the storytelling.

insights.claim: National Geographic's seven-episode series Africa: Earth's Wild Home took four years to make, was filmed across nearly 30 African countries, and is intended to launch a franchise covering all seven continents in turn.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Signals long-horizon investment in serial premium nature content as a repeatable franchise.

insights.claim: The series is streaming on Disney+ and Hulu, showing premium documentary content being used to fill Disney's streaming catalogs.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Library depth for streaming platforms; a minor retention lever rather than a driver.
insights.quote: Africa: Earth’s Wild Home is now streaming on Disney+ and Hulu.

insights.claim: The production leaned heavily on drones for first-person views and on a preprogrammed robotic camera arm, originally developed for studio use and deployed in the field for the first time.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Studio automation tools migrating to field production lowers the cost of repeatable long takes.

insights.claim: Custom remote rigs with low-light, infrared and remote zoom, plus an underwater pan/tilt hippo cam, enabled footage such as dwarf crocodiles hunting bats in a pitch-black cave.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Bespoke camera hardware is the moat for differentiated wildlife footage.

insights.claim: Each episode is split into mini-narratives, such as a mother cheetah adapting her hunting to rocky mountain terrain, and narrator Wunmi Mosaku deliberately used a natural, personable delivery rather than a put-on voice.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Character-driven storytelling is how nature documentaries are packaged for mainstream streaming audiences.
insights.quote: I wasn’t putting on a voice, it was very much Wunmi

insights.claim: The series claims the first TV appearance of the black rain frog and rare footage of chimpanzees using twigs as tools to fish for algae, as well as a hyena herding flamingos to catch one, described as a new skill for the species.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Exclusive first-seen footage is the marketing hook for the franchise.
